span: The only question before the criminal court is whether the cheque issued by the accused towards the discharge of his liability was dishonoured and despite the service of demand notice, whether he had not paid the amount
why: Court's reasoning treats service of the statutory demand notice and non-payment within 15 days as what makes the offence complete, so notice is part of the offence rather than optional.

span: The nature of the offence under Section 138 of the NI Act is quasi-criminal
why: Headnote on parallel prosecutions and the nature of the offence; nothing on demand notice.

span: in the absence of a notice of demand being served on the company and without compliance with the proviso to Section 138
why: Quoted extract on arraigning a company under s.141; the court says the issue is concluded by a larger bench but the passage itself does not show adoption on the demand-notice point.

span: thereafter the complainant has served demand notice to the accused

span: the payee or the holder in due course of the cheque, as the case may be, makes a demand for the payment of the said amount of money by giving a notice; in writing, to the drawer of the cheque
